summary:
Incomplete review: 1 of 9 checks could not be completed (Schedule Quality). The findings below cover only the checks that ran, so no overall score or assessment is given.

The proposal presents a coherent concept and a reasonably developed set of objectives, but it is not ready for submission. The insufficient bibliography is a critical compliance issue, while section-length violations, overlong paragraphs, passive phrasing, and incomplete AI transparency require substantial revision.

findings.title: Bibliography has fewer than the required minimum number of publications
findings.description: The bibliography contains only five publications ([TP21], [AAM17], [BBE10], [Bog+07], and [NM06]), while the guidelines require at least six to eight peer-reviewed publications. Add at least one additional relevant peer-reviewed publication, preferably several to reach the expected range.

locations.quote: [TP21] T. Tuononen and A. Parpala, “The Role of Academic Competences and Learning Processes in Predicting Bachelor's and Master's Thesis Grades,” Studies in Educational Evaluation, vol. 70, p. 101001, 2021, doi: 10.1016/j.stueduc.2021.101001.

findings.title: Problem section is too long
findings.description: The Problem section exceeds the maximum permitted length of three-quarters of a page. Condense the background, supporting explanation, and consequences to fit within the prescribed limit.

locations.quote: For students’ research proposals and theses, supervisors often provide feedback that is critical to their progress.
While the problem is less severe for students, they still experience its consequences.

findings.title: Motivation section is too long
findings.description: The Motivation section exceeds the maximum permitted length of three-quarters of a page and continues onto page 5. Reduce the explanatory detail and retain only the motivation most directly supporting the proposed work.

locations.quote: Integrating large language models (LLMs) to assist supervisors with non-content-related feedback could improve the thesis writing process.
Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs, students can obtain instant formative feedback at any point during the writing process.

findings.title: Several paragraphs are too long and combine multiple ideas
findings.description: Several paragraphs are too long and combine distinct ideas. Split the paragraph in section 4.1 into separate discussions of guideline representation and the rationale and limitations of formative feedback. Split the paragraph in section 4.2 into separate discussions of regression and persistent-issue definitions, adaptive feedback, and escalation to the supervisor.

locations.quote: Supervisors should be able to provide their own scientific writing guidelines as well as conventions on the style of theses and proposals. Based on these guidelines, the LLM can provide formative feedback that is restricted to the aspects they cover. Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format, the LLM may first need to preprocess them into a structured representation it can act on.

Ethically, it is difficult to let LLMs grade a final thesis, as this constitutes normative feedback and requires close scrutiny. Formative feedback, on the other hand, is less critical since it serves as input for students to improve their work.

If a regression occurs or an issue persists across iterations, the previous feedback was likely hard for the student to understand and act on. A regression means an aspect that was previously fine has worsened, while a persistent issue means earlier feedback flagged the same problem and the student has not yet resolved it.

In such cases, the feedback tool should adapt its style, for example by being more explanatory, more verbose, or providing concrete examples that illustrate the desired outcome. Where the feedback tool repeatedly fails to communicate an issue, it should defer the discussion to the supervisor.

findings.title: Repeated passive voice obscures responsibility
findings.description: Replace passive constructions with active sentences that identify the responsible actor, such as the student, supervisor, or feedback tool. Revise the cited instances to improve clarity and accountability.

locations.quote: Having to wait for feedback on purely formal aspects of a thesis or proposal can be frustrating for students, as these issues are governed by institutional conventions rather than research substance.
In one mode, no LLM-generated feedback is produced at all and all feedback comes from the supervisor.

In this combined mode, multiple specialized agents analyze specific parts of the thesis in parallel. The supervisor then aggregates and reviews the resulting feedback and adds their own feedback. Finally, the supervisor merges both sets and publishes them to the student, as illustrated in Figure 2.
At present, the feedback flow in Thesis Management only exists for the proposal, since the thesis is handed in as a single final submission without an iterative feedback cycle.

findings.title: Proposal sections using AI are not specified
findings.description: The AI Transparency Statement does not identify which proposal sections involved each AI tool. Revise it to name the relevant sections explicitly, such as the Abstract, Introduction, Motivation, Objectives, and Schedule, and associate each tool with its purpose in those sections.

locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across different stages of the writing process.

findings.title: Motivation repeats the Problem
findings.description: The Motivation section repeats the Problem rather than remaining exclusively visionary. Remove or substantially reframe references to the current repetitive feedback burden and supervisors being drained; describe the intended positive scientific and educational impact directly.

locations.quote: This Reviewer covers exactly the repetitive, non-content-related layer of feedback that currently drains supervisors, freeing them to focus on specific content and on discussions with their students.

findings.title: Revise filler transitions and forbidden sentence starters
findings.description: Edit sentence-level style throughout the cited sections. Remove transitional fillers such as “Moreover,” “Additionally,” and “In addition” when they add no meaning, and recast sentences beginning with “As,” “Because,” or “Since” so that they begin with the main subject or claim.

locations.quote: Moreover, the time spent on repetitive feedback leaves less time for what matters most: helping students with their research and providing feedback on substantive topics.
Additionally, supervisors can provide feedback faster, making the process more scalable.

As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group’s writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback [NM06].
Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs, students can obtain instant formative feedback at any point during the writing process.
Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format, the LLM may first need to preprocess them into a structured representation it can act on.
In addition, privacy regulations and cost require careful consideration of when to use locally self-hosted LLMs versus cloud-hosted ones.

findings.title: Undefined abbreviation “AI”
findings.description: Define “AI” as “artificial intelligence” at first use or replace the abbreviation with the full term for readers who may not know it.

locations.quote: The supervisor then revises the AI-generated draft, joins it with their own feedback, and publishes the result to the student.
In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools across different stages of the writing process.

findings.title: Several paragraphs are too short to develop their ideas
findings.description: Improve paragraph structure by incorporating the two-line introduction paragraph into the preceding paragraph or expanding it to explain the thesis's role in the lifecycle. Also combine the standalone one- and two-line Schedule introduction paragraphs into one concise introductory paragraph or expand them to explain how the schedule is organized.

locations.quote: The student, by contrast, hands in the thesis itself as a single final submission.
The Bachelor thesis starts on 26.06.2026 and the submission is on 26.10.2026.
We divided the time into several two-week iterations, each containing tasks to fulfill the overall goals:

findings.title: Correct heading capitalization and standardize LLM terminology
findings.description: Correct the heading capitalization to “Integrate with Thesis Management” and use consistent terminology for large language models throughout the document. Avoid the redundant expression “LLM Models” and select one form, such as “LLM” or “LLM models,” according to context.
